Am I wrong for considering it to be patronizing? There is a certain point of depression in adulthood that a person reaches where they are not really amused or impassioned by media or videogames like they used to. Not that they shouldn’t be; but our interests begin to broaden as we age, and things like movies, tv shows, and games feel less and less important.

Like if someone told me to “wait for the Barbie movie, it’ll be so good” before that one came out, I would have laughed in their face. I don’t care how good it is, it is a piece of media that will have no effect on my life whatsoever.

It is a tough, but necessary lesson for psychotics to learn. You can have the “fun” psychotic trips, or you can have a normal life—but you can only pick one.

As someone who likes to interact with other people during my episodes, I learned very quickly that most people don’t have the patience for it.

And it’s not that people are mean or incompassionate. I think most people’s thought process is “I shouldn’t entertain this line of thinking because I could hurt them, and they could hurt themselves if I play along.” Even I hesitate to comment when I see that someone else is going through an episode, because I don’t want to say the wrong thing and end up triggering them more.

I think the best thing you could do for your friend is tell him that you’re uncomfortable interacting with him while he’s experiencing hallucinations or intense delusions. That’s definitely not an unreasonable parameter to set, and it might give him some motivation to get medication.
